newsitem.title: UK: NWE FUEL OIL BARGES STEADY, CARGOES OFFERED STRONG.
newsitem.headline: NWE FUEL OIL BARGES STEADY, CARGOES OFFERED STRONG.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil barges were little changed in a quiet early market on Friday as a major buyer declined to meet sellers' higher numbers, while cracked cargoes were offered $3 stronger.
High sulphur fuel barges traded at least twice at $94.50 fob ARA for RMG material. A major buyer bid $95 for refinery product but sellers were standing their ground at $95.50.

The major bought on Thursday at $95, which was followed by a deal at $95.50. "We have a feeling that he did not want to be booked but rather support the market," a trader said, reflecting the view of other market players.

Tight high sulphur cracked fuel cargoes was talked higher, with one trader showing a cargo at $88 fob, or $3 over what it paid for it earlier this week. Buyers, however, were said to be uninterested at this level.
"They'll probably let them sit at that price. They're asking for a higher price simply because they have already paid a high price for the cargo," a trader said.
For Russian cracked cargoes, traders said that the high end of offers was in the two means plus $2 region, or unchanged.
"The Russian material has come down from about $3 (over the two means quote) earlier this week," a trader said.
One percent continued to be offered in the $96/$97 region, reflecting the level of swaps, traders said.
